text.p: The Federal Reserve on Thursday approved a proposal by National Westminster Bank Plc to take over Greenwich Capital Holdings Inc and engage in a wide range of non-banking activities.
Connecticut-based Greenwich Capital, previously owned by Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd, will remain a broker-dealer registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
As a result of the acquisition, NatWest will be able to provide discount and full-service securities brokering.
NatWest also will be able to provide services such as investment advice and underwriting and dealing in municipal revenue bonds.
NatWest already has branches in New York and Chicago and controls several subsidiaries that engage in various non-banking activities.
The Fed said the takeover of Greenwich "would provide added convenience, a broader array of products and improved services to NatWest's customers."
